A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure raise the share of lung cancer patients who get curative-intent treatment, and by how much?
Measure: Thoracic surgeon reviews every decision not to operate. A thoracic surgeon from the university hospital sits in the county lung meeting every week and gives a second opinion before a stage I-II patient is refused surgery. Counties without their own thoracic surgeon decide about surgery without one today.
effect_summary_en: An observational English study found more operations where surgeons were based (20.0% vs 11.6%); the abstract does not give a figure for surgeons attending the meeting.
supported_en: Lau et al. (J Thorac Oncol 2013) found a higher resection rate in hospitals that had their own surgeons: 20.0% vs 11.6%.
not_supported_en: The abstract does not show the 2.4-point gain from surgeons attending the meeting, and it does not show that the link is causal.
in_use_quote: Tyksissä kokoontuu viikoittain moniammatillinen työryhmä, joka tarvittaessa käsittelee tutkimustulokset ja suunnittelee hoitolinjauksesi. Kokouksessa on läsnä keuhkosairauksien erikoislääkäreitä sekä kirurgian, sädehoidon, patologian ja radiologian erikoislääkärit.
missing_en: No page says that every stage I-II patient who is refused surgery is reviewed by a thoracic surgeon.
summary_en: Tyks says a team meets every week with lung doctors, surgeons, radiotherapy, pathology and radiology specialists, and Satasairaala doctors join it by video. Tyks also says not every cancer case needs to go to the meeting, and Satakunta's own page says a lung surgeon is one of the doctors who plans treatment. On the effect, the 2013 English study (Lau et al.) is observational: hospitals with their own surgeons operated more often (20.0% vs 11.6%), and the abstract we read does not give the 14.4% vs 12.0% figure for surgeons attending the meeting.
unanswered_en: I found no page saying whether Satasairaala operates on lung cancer itself, and none on how the decision not to operate is reviewed.
